decisionsTitle: `yarn ship` waits only on the checks GitHub requires
decisionsSection:
**What happened.** On the night of 2026-10-10/11 `yarn ship` merged nothing for over twenty minutes: it polled «waiting on 1 check(s): Vercel – <the QA project>» on the release PR. That status is Vercel's QA project reporting on the head of `qa`; the QA deployment had happened long before, and GitHub did not require it — `mergeStateStatus` said `UNSTABLE`, mergeable with a non-required status not green. The dispatcher stopped the ship and merged by hand. §504 and §658 had made the ship say what it waits on; neither asked whether anyone required it, and §426's release-PR rule (stop on any failed check but a Vercel one, wait on every pending one) is what this replaces.

**Decision.** The release PR's wait is `scripts/pr-merge-gate.mjs`, a pure judgement of the PR's `mergeStateStatus`, its `statusCheckRollup` and the contexts that are required: GitHub's list joined with the house's own four (`tested-tree`, `docs-check`, `e2e`, `migrate`). GitHub's list is read at each poll with `gh pr checks --required`, which needs only pull-request read — the phone's `SHIP_TOKEN` has no Administration permission (`SETUP.md` §41), so branch protection is only a second source; when neither answers the poll prints once «required list unreadable — using the house's checks». A sharded house check (`e2e 3/8`) counts as its aggregate (`e2e`), which registers only after every shard ends, so a pending or red shard holds or stops the release PR; a house check that has not registered is waited for unless GitHub says `CLEAN` or `HAS_HOOKS`. Mergeable: every required context that has registered concluded SUCCESS, SKIPPED or NEUTRAL, and the state is `CLEAN`, `UNSTABLE` or `HAS_HOOKS`. Waiting: a required context pending, the state `UNKNOWN`, or a required context not yet registered while GitHub still blocks. Stop, with the reason: `DIRTY` (conflicts), `BEHIND` («update the branch»), a failed required check. Every poll (each thirty seconds) prints `waiting on: <name> (required|not required)…`, and a not-required status that was open at the merge is named. The migration wait, production's waits (§658) and the time records (§504) are unchanged; the batch PR keeps the §426 wait on all its checks, which carries no Vercel status. This amends §426: its criterion 10 sentence about the release PR (stop on any failed or cancelled check except a Vercel deployment check) is replaced by this gate; the rest of §426 stands.

**Refused.** Hardcoding the Vercel projects' names — the rule is «what GitHub requires», so a project added or renamed changes nothing here. `gh pr merge --admin` — it would merge past a failed required check as readily as past a status nobody requires.
changelogLine: - **`yarn ship` waits only on the checks GitHub requires** — a Vercel status on the release PR no longer holds the merge; each poll says what it waits on and whether it is required. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Given `yarn ship` and the `qa → main` release PR, when it waits to merge, then it reads the PR's `mergeStateStatus` and `statusCheckRollup` and the contexts GitHub requires on `main`, and merges once every required context has concluded SUCCESS, SKIPPED or NEUTRAL and the state is `CLEAN`, `UNSTABLE` or `HAS_HOOKS`; a `Vercel – *` status that is not required is named and never waited on, neither pending nor red; it waits while a required context is pending or the state is `UNKNOWN`, and stops with a reason on `DIRTY`, `BEHIND` or a failed required check; the house's `tested-tree`, `docs-check`, `e2e` and `migrate` are required beside whatever GitHub lists, read with `gh pr checks --required`, and when the list cannot be read the poll says so once; each poll prints `waiting on: <name> (required|not required)…`. This replaces the release-PR sentence of criterion 10 (§426). Verification: unit `tests/unit/scripts/pr-merge-gate.test.ts` (2026-10-11, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

batchLine: the ship waits on required checks only
